players.product: electrical and mechanical construction and installation of data-center power and cooling systems

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 revenues were a quarterly record of $4.5 billion, up 19.7% (9.5% organically), with a 9.7% non-GAAP operating margin. U.S. Electrical Construction revenues were a record $1.36 billion, up 45.8% (organic growth plus the Miller acquisition); its data center projects in network and communications grew nearly 50% year over year, and CFO Jason Nalbandian said half of the segment's growth came from data centers. U.S. Mechanical Construction revenues were a record $1.94 billion, up 17%, with network and communications revenues up nearly 80%. Full-year 2025 revenues were $16.99 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenues $4.5 billion (+19.7%); Electrical Construction $1.36 billion (+45.8%), network and communications nearly 50%; Mechanical Construction $1.94 billion (+17%), network and communications nearly 80%; FY2025 revenues $16.99 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Tony Guzzi: RPOs within network and communications (where the data center business sits) reached a record $4.46 billion at the end of December, up $1.65 billion or nearly 60% year over year. 'We see no change in the momentum of the CapEx plans from our customers in this sector, and we have good visibility for the next 2 to 3 years as we work to support their build-out.' Asked about the analyst-cited 33% network and communications share of RPO, Guzzi said it could be 40% or 45% for a period or go down to 30% depending on demand and mix; in the Electrical segment it is 40% to 50% and 'may even go up a little bit'. CFO: RPO counts only funded phases of a data center campus, and 82% of it will burn over the next 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: network and communications RPO record $4.46 billion (+$1.65 billion, nearly 60% YoY); 40% to 50% in Electrical segment; 82% burns over next 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 guidance: revenues of $17.75 billion to $18.5 billion, diluted EPS of $27.25 to $29.25 and an operating margin between 9% and 9.4%. To reach the mid-to-high end EMCOR needs to book 40% to 45% of new work; 'we see no slowing of demand for most of our end markets and continue to see exceptional prospects in our data center markets.' CFO: the U.K. sale is a 3% revenue headwind offset by the Miller and Danforth acquisitions, so essentially all guided growth is organic.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenues $17.75 billion to $18.5 billion; EPS $27.25 to $29.25; operating margin between 9% and 9.4%; must book 40% to 45% of new work

quarterly_data.signal: Guzzi on why data center growth is faster in mechanical than electrical: 'We're benefiting more from the AI data center ... the scope doesn't increase as much going from a 100-megawatt cloud storage data center to a 200-megawatt AI data center on the electrical side. But on the mechanical side, it can be a 1.5 to 2x multiplier on the mechanical systems that will go in.' CFO: in dollars Electrical still grew more in 2025 ($1 billion) than Mechanical ($850 million).
quarterly_data.figure: AI data center = 1.5 to 2x multiplier on mechanical systems vs cloud data center; 2025 growth Electrical $1 billion, Mechanical $850 million

quarterly_data.signal: Guzzi: EMCOR can operate in about 17 data center markets electrically and about 7 mechanically, and can cover the whole country in fire life safety; it is a national data center player electrically but still 'a super regional player' mechanically. Data center markets are now set by 'this quest for power, right, quest for stranded power' (its Indiana electrical contractor followed stranded power from former steel mills and auto plants); he expects a couple more markets to be added and denser builds in existing hubs such as Northern Virginia, Columbus, Chicago, Arizona, Atlanta and Dallas.
quarterly_data.figure: about 17 markets electrically; about 7 markets now mechanically

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor fab work: high-tech manufacturing RPO has grown at a 48% compound annual rate since 12/31/19, and Guzzi remains 'very bullish on this market with the demand for semiconductor chips'. Q4 mechanical high-tech manufacturing revenue fell because certain semiconductor projects were completed. New semiconductor awards now come in smaller chunks: where EMCOR might once have received a $150 million award, customers in Arizona (EMCOR works for 2 of the customers there) now let the work out '$30 million, $50 million at a time'.
quarterly_data.figure: high-tech manufacturing RPO CAGR 48%; awards of $30 million, $50 million at a time vs a $150 million award previously
